BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). ## Executive view

The Seller’s package departs materially from the Buyer playbook. It reallocates substantial risk to Wattlebridge through lower caps, much higher thresholds, shorter limitation periods, broad deemed disclosure and knowledge exclusions, and an attempted extension of the general limitations regime to title, indemnities, covenants and other claims.

We should not accept the liability package as drafted. Bluefen, Riverlark, the employee bonuses and Ironquay also require substantive completion mechanics rather than disclosure alone.

## Detailed review

| Issue | Seller position | Departure / risk | Buyer pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General Warranty cap** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Our starting position is 25% / AUD 6m. The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying this draft; none has been given. | Reinstate **25% / AUD 6m**. Do not accept or describe 20% as agreed without Amelia’s written authority. |
| **De minimis** | AUD 25,000 | Five times our position and liable to exclude individually meaningful claims. | **AUD 5,000**. Appropriate aggregation rules should prevent artificial splitting of related matters. |
| **Basket** | AUD 250,000, with only excess recoverable | Five times our basket and changes it from a tipping basket to a deductible. | **AUD 50,000 tipping basket**: once exceeded, Seller liable from the first dollar for qualifying claims. |
| **General claims period** | 18 months | Our position is 24 months. Eighteen months is an approval-only fallback and no approval exists. It may expire before latent issues emerge or a full audit cycle is completed. | Reinstate **24 months after Completion**. |
| **Fundamental, capacity and Title claims** | Same cap and period as general warranties | Unacceptable. It could leave Buyer with only AUD 4.8m recovery if Seller did not own or could not sell the shares. It also conflicts with the premise of acquiring 100% ownership. | Separate regime: **100% of price cap**, at least **six years**, and outside all general baskets, de minimis thresholds and knowledge exclusions. Include ownership, title, encumbrances, authority, capacity and valid issuance. |
| **“All Claims” limitation language** | General limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded | Creates a hidden override of separately negotiated protections, potentially covering indemnities, repayment obligations, covenants, Tax, IP and Completion payments. | Limit the general regime expressly to **General Warranty Claims only**. Create separate, explicit regimes for Title/fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenant claims. |
| **Fraud and deliberate conduct** | Caps, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all claims | No carve-out is stated. This could purport to protect Seller against fraud or concealment. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of **all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy provisions, non-reliance language and other limitations**, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-waivable. |
| **Exclusive remedy / non-reliance** | Applies to all claims of any nature | Overbroad and especially problematic for indemnities, debt recovery, specific performance, equitable relief, fraud and pre-Completion covenants. | Confine it to the agreed general warranty regime, with express exclusions for fraud and deliberate conduct, Title, Tax, IP, indemnities, payment obligations, covenants, equitable relief and rights that cannot lawfully be excluded. |
| **General disclosure** | Entire data room, statutory registers and public records deemed disclosed | Directly contrary to our requirement for specific fair disclosure. It shifts the review burden to Buyer and may qualify warranties through obscure or incomplete material. | Delete clauses 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Require each matter to be **specifically and fairly disclosed against the relevant warranty**, with sufficient detail to identify its nature, scope and reasonably foreseeable implications. No prudent-search, public-register or whole-data-room deemed disclosure. |
| **Buyer knowledge** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from data room or public records | An expansive actual, imputed and constructive knowledge bar. Adviser knowledge could be attributed across a large diligence team, and “discoverable” converts disclosure into a search obligation. | Delete the blanket exclusion. At most, consider a tightly defined actual-knowledge provision limited to named senior Buyer individuals, without adviser attribution or constructive knowledge—but never for Title, capacity, fraud, deliberate conduct or a specific indemnity. Seller warranty knowledge qualifiers should identify named Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. |
| **Disclosure letter reservation** | No admission of breach, liability, materiality or legal requirement | A factual non-admission is not itself objectionable, but it cannot prevent disclosed facts from engaging contractual obligations or agreed risk allocation. | Clarify that the reservation does not qualify the SPA, negate warranties or indemnities, or make otherwise inadequate disclosure fair. |
| **Disclosure cut-off** | Data room as at 5.00pm on 22 September 2026 | The disclosure set may be stale. Matters arising or changing after that date are not addressed. | Require an updated disclosure bundle through signing and a controlled Completion bring-down. No new disclosure after signing should qualify warranties without Buyer’s express written acceptance and, where appropriate, a termination or remedy right. |

## Transaction-specific matters

### 1. Bluefen consent — critical Completion condition

Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, or about 30%. The disclosure confirms that there is currently neither final written consent nor evidence that the contractual conditions have been satisfied.

“Reasonable endeavours” and deemed satisfaction merely upon delivery of a consent are inadequate because:

- consent may be conditional, revocable or ineffective;
- clause 11.3 conditions may remain unsatisfied;
- an adverse consent condition could materially change the economics or customer relationship; and
- this is a concentrated, material customer dependency.

**Pushback:** Completion must be conditional on:

1. effective written consent from the proper Bluefen counterparty;
2. evidence satisfactory to Buyer that all conditions to that consent have been satisfied or irrevocably waived;
3. no materially adverse amendment, fee, concession or other condition without Buyer approval; and
4. the consent remaining effective at Completion.

The condition should not be deemed satisfied merely by document delivery.

### 2. Riverlark facility and security — critical Completion mechanic

The Seller proposes a release after Completion, while the disclosure confirms approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding and no final discharge is available. That is inconsistent with a debt-free acquisition and could leave the target encumbered after ownership transfers.

**Pushback:**

- obtain a current payout letter close to Completion;
- pay Riverlark directly from Completion funds;
- obtain effective releases and discharges of all target and share security at Completion;
- confirm closure or agreed treatment of the facility and related guarantees; and
- reflect the repayment expressly in the funds flow and debt-free/cash-free calculation.

A post-Completion release is not acceptable absent an irrevocable bank undertaking in an agreed form and Amelia Frost’s written approval. No such approval presently exists.

### 3. Employee bonuses

DD-005 identifies AUD 420,000 of Completion-triggered bonuses, but they are omitted from the funds flow and the on-cost position is unknown. Calling them “a matter for the Seller” does not ensure that the Company or Buyer will not bear the cash, payroll tax, superannuation or related costs after Completion.

**Pushback:**

- quantify bonuses and all applicable on-costs;
- include them as a specific funds-flow line item;
- require payment or full funding by Seller;
- ensure they do not reduce target cash delivered to Buyer or become a post-Completion target liability; and
- obtain evidence of payment, withholding and required superannuation/payroll-tax treatment.

### 4. Ironquay IP

The proposed indemnity is too narrow if limited to the SOW3 payment. DD-004 suggests transfer of Project Materials is conditional on payment of all SOW3 fees, but the AUD 180,000 entry is not independently verified and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.

**Pushback:**

- retain a cure mechanism allowing verified payment of any properly due SOW3 amount;
- independently confirm the amount and payee;
- require evidence of cleared payment and effective assignment/vesting of all relevant IP;
- broaden the indemnity to cover losses arising from non-payment, failure of transfer, ownership defects, encumbrances and third-party claims connected with the Ironquay work; and
- preserve specific performance and other remedies.

We should not assume either that AUD 180,000 is payable or that payment alone cures every IP issue.

### 5. Export/privacy incident

The disclosure is appropriately cautious: it does not establish access, a confirmed breach, notification duty, harm or loss. We should neither accept the Seller’s assertion that it is immaterial nor assert an unsupported breach or monetary demand.

**Pushback / diligence actions:**

- immediate preservation of access, download, email, authentication and system logs;
- a documented investigation by appropriately qualified personnel;
- regular written updates and prompt notice of material developments;
- preservation of evidence and no admission or notification without appropriate consultation, subject to mandatory law;
- confirmation of containment and remediation; and
- appropriate warranty and, depending on findings, a tailored indemnity or escrow.

Any notification decision should be evidence-based and comply with applicable privacy and other laws.

### 6. Sandbar renewals

The Seller characterises AUD 330,000 of renewals as ordinary-course costs, but the disclosure expressly does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Pushback:** Obtain the three contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, service periods, payment status and accounting treatment. Do not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct them from price. Their treatment should follow the agreed definitions and evidence—potentially as ordinary-course expenditure, working capital, accruals, commitments or another category.

### 7. Title evidence

DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal register, not independent proof of title. It does not by itself establish valid issuance, beneficial ownership, absence of encumbrances or authority to transfer.

**Pushback:** Require independent corroboration, including:

- ASIC/company searches and historical filings;
- constitution and relevant corporate approvals;
- original or replacement share certificates and transfer history;
- confirmation of issued capital and absence of options or other rights;
- PPSR and other relevant encumbrance searches;
- releases of share and asset security; and
- Seller and Company board approvals and authority evidence.

The Title warranties must remain independent of disclosure and Buyer knowledge.

### 8. Office lease and Mossvale

The current disclosure does not show that landlord consent or Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold. We should not turn either into an unnecessary Completion condition without reviewing the operative provisions.

However, any actual notice obligations should be identified and allocated, and the Seller should covenant to make required notifications in the correct form and within the contractual period.

### 9. Tax and IP remain open

The Seller cannot unilaterally declare Tax and IP “settled” under the general regime. Under our instructions, these terms remain open, with no assumption of either unlimited liability or agreed resolution.

**Pushback:** Continue negotiating separate Tax and IP warranties, indemnities, limitations, claim periods and conduct provisions. They must not be inadvertently swept into the proposed AUD 4.8m/18-month general regime.

## Recommended negotiation priorities

### Non-negotiable protections

1. Full carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
2. Separate Title/fundamental regime: 100% cap, at least six years, no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
3. Delete whole-data-room, public-register and “discoverable matter” disclosure.
4. Remove the blanket Buyer/adviser knowledge exclusion.
5. Prevent general limitations from applying to all claim categories.

### Key economic positions

6. Restore the AUD 6m general Warranty cap.
7. Restore AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket.
8. Restore the 24-month general claim period.
9. Make the AUD 420,000 bonuses and triggered on-costs expressly Seller-funded.
10. Implement Riverlark repayment and security releases through the Completion funds flow.

### Completion and diligence protections

11. Make effective Bluefen consent, including satisfaction of its conditions, a genuine Completion condition.
12. Obtain independent Title and encumbrance evidence.
13. Verify and cure the Ironquay IP position, supported by a broader indemnity.
14. Preserve evidence and complete the export/privacy investigation without prejudging its outcome.
15. Investigate Sandbar treatment rather than automatically treating it as Debt or a price adjustment.
16. Require refreshed disclosure through signing/Completion and retain Tax and IP as expressly open items.

Overall, the Seller’s draft should be treated as a substantial risk-transfer proposal, not a fair or settled package.
